Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-16-0**

### New in 0.16.2

#### Fixed

- **Bulk-deleting hundreds of device types works, and reads right in the change log.** A type's component templates were each logged on the way out, so 800 library types with dozens of ports each were tens of thousands of change-log rows in one request - the worker was killed before it finished and nothing was deleted. The delete now writes one entry per type, carrying the templates it had, and the cascade runs without the per-row logging: a hundred 48-port types go in half a second instead of seventeen. The Device types page also sends a big selection in batches of a hundred. (#178)
- **A POST to a backend that is down answers 503, not nginx's own 405 page.** The maintenance page nginx shows while the backend restarts is a static file, which nginx will not serve for a POST; an API call that met it got a bare "405 Not Allowed". The shipped nginx template now answers such a request with a JSON 503 that says what happened. (#178)
- **The Prefixes, VLANs, Sites and Aggregates lists cost the same whatever their size.** Each did one or more queries per row - a scan of every prefix per prefix for its child count, a prefix count per VLAN, nine counts per site, a walk over every prefix per aggregate - so a tenant with a few hundred objects waited seconds and a few thousand waited minutes. Every figure those lists show is now computed once per page, and a test holds the query count flat between a page of five and a page of thirty. (#179, #180, #181)

#### Upgrading

- The nginx change is in the template: on a systemd install run `sudo make proxy-install` once to render it again (the installer does it on a fresh install); a hand-managed nginx config wants the same `if ($request_method !~ ^(GET|HEAD)$)` branch in its maintenance location.
